chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Al-Halby, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed li'an (mutual cursing) with his wife while she was pregnant. So when she gave birth, he claimed her child and acknowledged it and asserted that it was from him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'His child is returned to him, and he does not inherit him, and he is not whipped, because the li'an has passed.'
ai.seo_question: What are the inheritance and punishment rulings for a father who claims his child after performing li'an with a pregnant wife?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while the li'an process severs the automatic inheritance link between father and child, the father retains custody and paternity acknowledgment. The exemption from re-whipping highlights the principle that the li'an ceremony is a singular, conclusive legal act, preventing double punishment for the same oath. This distinction underscores the precision of Shia jurisprudence in balancing marital dispute resolution with inheritance rights.
